backlogItem: MIRROR the piece-square tables per color
change: getPieceValueSum now mirrors the board index (rank r -> 7-r) for black pieces, so Black reads the piece-square tables from its own perspective instead of White's. evaluate() gains a `mirror` flag (default true) and negamax() an optional `evaluateFn` so the harness can A/B new vs legacy from a single eval source.
reason: Net-positive and non-regressing across ~700 seeded games at depths 2 and 3, and a genuine correctness fix (Black's positional evaluation was vertically inverted). Color-symmetry unit tests confirm evaluate() is now side-symmetric. Bundle well under the 45KB brotli limit.

change: negamax default leaf evaluator is now quiescentEval: at the search horizon it resolves pending captures via a stand-pat negamax (MVV-LVA ordered, delta-pruned with a 200cp promotion-aware margin, self-check-filtered, capture-promotions auto-queened) before scoring. Fixes the horizon effect where the static evaluate() was taken mid-exchange and mis-counted material. Harness updated: newEval=quiescentEval, legacyEval=static mirrored evaluate() (the previous accepted engine), isolating the quiescence contribution. En passant and check-evasions are intentionally omitted (standard qsearch simplification); mate is still scored by negamax at its own nodes.
review: adversarial subagent review: all 9 correctness checks pass; delta-pruning soundness fuzz-verified (0 mismatches across ~30k legal positions); self-check/pin filter and sign convention confirmed empirically
reason: Large, robust strength gain that is also a genuine correctness improvement (eliminates horizon-effect blunders). Non-regressing and strongly net-positive across 560 seeded games from varied openings, both colors: 88.9% at depth 2 (400 games) and 93.1% at depth 3 (160 games), across two seeds each, with near-zero losses (11L/6L). Two new unit tests pin the behavior (declines a poisoned capture, grabs a winning one). Bundle 6.81KB brotli, far under the 45KB limit.

change: Added a pawn-structure term (doubled -12/extra file, isolated -14, passed-pawn bonus rising by rank) as pawnStructureDelta(board) = White-minus-Black, layered onto the static eval via a new evaluateFull() used as the production quiescence leaf. evaluate() itself was left structure-free; the quiescence stand-pat gained a pawnStructure flag so the harness could A/B new=quiescence+structure (quiescentEval->evaluateFull) vs legacy=quiescence-only (quiescentEvalNoStructure, the experiment #2 engine). Correctness pinned by exact-value + color-symmetry unit tests.

depth3_afterOffByOneFix.note: Fixed an off-by-one that zeroed the 7th-rank passed bonus (PASSED_BONUS[7]=0) and peaked it at the 6th; raising the 7th-rank bonus to 130 made depth-3 strictly worse (41.9%->36.9%), a clean monotonic trend: more passed-pawn weight => weaker play.

rootCause: The passed-pawn incentive makes this shallow-search engine chase/advance passers it cannot convert within the horizon, conceding material and tactics that the structure-blind baseline then punishes. The effect is depth-dependent (neutral at depth 2, clear regression at depth 3) and worsens monotonically as the passer bonus grows, so it is the eval term steering the search wrong, not a tuning accident. Color symmetry and starting-position=0 were unit-verified, ruling out an asymmetry bug.
reason: Fails the self-play NON-REGRESSION gate at depth 3 under two independent tunings (41.9% then 36.9% over 160 games/seed). All other gate checks (typecheck/lint/format/tests/build/size 7.06KB) passed, but per the gate a strength regression must be fixed or fully reverted; the one available fix made it worse, so the change was fully reverted to the experiment #2 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. Lesson for future runs: a naive pawn-structure term (especially the passed-pawn bonus) is counterproductive for this engine at the UI's search depths. Revisit only with much smaller weights, gated on the pawn being safely advanceable, or after a search-depth / king-safety improvement — and always validate at depth 3+, not just depth 2.

change: Horizon-only check extension in negamax. Quiescence resolves captures at the leaf but not check evasions, so a leaf reached with the side to move in check is scored by a stand-pat that cannot tell a forced mate/loss from a harmless check. Now when the search reaches the horizon (depth<=0) in check, it extends one ply to search the (few, forced) evasions instead of trusting the leaf. Interior nodes are unchanged, so only in-check frontier leaves pay the cost. A per-path budget (CHECK_EXTENSION_BUDGET) bounds a run of consecutive frontier checks. Also refactored negamax to keep it under the eslint complexity cap: extracted resolveSearchDepth() (the extension decision) and orderMoves() (MVV-LVA move ordering) as pure helpers, and reused a single isInCheck() for both the extension and the mate branch. Harness A/B: both engines use the accepted quiescence leaf (experiment #2); new=checkExtend true, old=checkExtend false, threaded via new per-side whiteCheckExtend/blackCheckExtend playGame flags in runMatch's two color-swapped calls.
budgetPivot: Started at CHECK_EXTENSION_BUDGET=3. At the UI's DEFAULT depth 4, the 3-ply check-chains caused pathological worst-case search time on rare alternating-check positions: every budget-3 depth-4 self-play process was repeatedly killed mid-run (exit 144/1, empty output), while budget-1 and all depth-2/3 runs completed. Reduced to budget=1 (a single extension ply, no chains): bounded cost, reliably completes at depth 4, and strength-equivalent to budget=3 at these depths because check-chains are rare (budget-1 and budget-3 produced byte-identical results at depth 3 seed 1 = 48.3% 20W-18D-22L, and identical depth-2 aggregates = 58.9%). Shipped budget=1; a larger budget would occasionally freeze the AI mid-move in the browser.

selfPlay.note: All figures are the SHIPPED engine (budget 1) vs the previous accepted engine (experiment #2, no check extension); seeds use disjoint opening sets. Score: win=1 draw=0.5.

review: Adversarial subagent review of the diff: all 7 correctness properties pass — bounded recursion/termination (total depth <= nominal + budget), negamax sign convention, mate scoring (interior mates unchanged; -50000-searchDepth), A/B isolation across BOTH color swaps, production default preserved (checkExtend defaults true), repetition + alpha-beta window intact, and the unit-test mate position is a true mate-in-1. No bugs. One inherent, benign note: horizon mates all score -50001 regardless of true distance — never misses a mate or prefers a non-mate.
reason: Non-regressing and net-positive across 610 seeded games from varied openings, both colors, at every depth the UI actually plays — depth 2 58.9% (400g), depth 3 52.9% (120g), and the DEFAULT depth 4 62.8% (90g) — and a genuine correctness improvement (in-check horizon leaves are resolved instead of mis-scored by a capture-only stand-pat). Validated at depth 3+ per the experiment #3 lesson, not just depth 2. A reliability/cost risk (pathological depth-4 search time) was found and fixed by capping the extension at one ply; the budget-3 variant was reverted for that reason. All gate checks green, bundle 6.72KB brotli (well under 45KB). A new unit test pins that a mate-in-1 delivered by a checking move — invisible to a plain depth-1 search whose mating child sits at the un-searched depth-0 horizon — is found once the in-check horizon is extended.

change: Tapered king piece-square table. The king was scored from a single middlegame table (AI.kingTable) at every game phase; the endgame table (AI.kingTableEndGame) was defined but never read, so the engine kept its king cowering on the back rank even in pawn endgames where an active, centralised king is worth ~1-2 pawns of practical strength. Added gamePhaseMg(board) (standard 24-point phase: N/B=1, R=2, Q=4 both colors, pawns/kings excluded, capped at 24) returning a middlegame weight in [0,1], and kingSquareValue(idx,mgWeight) blending kingTable*mg + kingTableEndGame*(1-mg) (rounded). evaluate() gains a `tapered` flag (default false) that computes mgWeight once and threads it to both getPieceValueSum calls; quiesce() threads `tapered` into its stand-pat evaluate() and every recursive child; new leaf quiescentEvalTapered = quiescence with tapering on. At mgWeight>=1 (full material) kingSquareValue returns kingTable[idx] exactly, so the shipped non-tapered leaf (quiescentEval / production negamax default) is byte-for-byte unchanged. Harness A/B: newEval=quiescentEvalTapered vs legacyEval=quiescentEval (the experiment #4 engine); both check-extend true (shipped). Correctness pinned by color-symmetry and endgame-centralisation unit tests.

selfPlay.note: new = tapered-king leaf, old = middlegame-only king leaf (experiment #4). Both use quiescence + shipped check extensions. Disjoint opening seeds (spaced >= games/2 apart). Score: win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for new.

review: Adversarial subagent review of the diff: all 6 correctness properties PASS (verdict SHIP). (1) backward-compat: non-tapered path byte-for-byte unchanged (kingSquareValue(idx,1) returns kingTable[idx] exactly; quiescentEval and production negamax default untouched); (2) color symmetry preserved (phase is color-independent, both kings taper with the same mgWeight via their own mirrored index, so a symmetric position scores 0); (3) phase math correct (24-scale, capped so promotions can't exceed weight 1, pawns/kings excluded, iterates real squares only); (4) taper threaded through the stand-pat and all quiescence recursion with no path reverting mid-search; (5) delta-pruning still sound (both king tables in ~[-50,+40], positional swing under DELTA_MARGIN 200); (6) Math.round cannot introduce color asymmetry (identical args per side). No bug found.
reason: Non-regressing and net-positive across 560 seeded games from varied openings, both colors, at every depth the UI plays -- depth 2 52.9% (240g), depth 3 54.2% (240g), and the DEFAULT depth 4 60.0% (80g, all four seeds positive) -- with the effect strongest at the production depth, exactly where deeper search reaches and plays out the endgames the tapered king improves. Validated at depth 3+ per the experiment #3 lesson; only 1 of 13 seed-matches fell below 50% (depth-3 seed 41 at 42.5%, within the known large depth-3 variance) and the aggregate at every depth is >= 52.9%. Also a genuine correctness/completeness fix: it activates the endgame king table that was defined but never read, valuing the king for safety in the middlegame and activity in the endgame instead of hiding it on the back rank all game. All gate checks green; bundle 6.99KB brotli (far under the 45KB limit); adversarial diff review passed 6/6. Unlike the rejected pawn-structure term (#3), tapering induces no committal pawn pushes -- it only relocates the king's ideal square as material comes off, so it cannot steer the shallow search into unconvertible chases.

change: Bishop-pair bonus: a side holding two or more bishops gets +40cp (BISHOP_PAIR_BONUS), added via bishopPairDelta(board,color) = White-minus-Black from the side-to-move's perspective. Threaded behind a `bishopPair` flag (default false) through evaluate() and quiesce() so every existing caller (quiescentEval, quiescentEvalTapered) is byte-for-byte unchanged; the quiescence delta-pruning margin is widened by the bonus only when the flag is on. New production leaf quiescentEvalBishopPair = quiescence + tapered king + bishop-pair. The engine previously valued two bishops identically to bishop+knight (materially wrong by ~half a pawn); this is a non-committal correctness fix — it biases roughly equal minor-piece trades toward keeping the pair but never pushes a piece to a worse square, so unlike the rejected passed-pawn term (#3) it cannot steer the shallow search into unconvertible material.
shippingFix: Also finally ships experiment #5 (tapered king eval). #5 was accepted in the lab but its commit (61bfd77) never changed negamax's default evaluateFn from the non-tapered quiescentEval, and makeAIMove uses the default — so the browser AI had been running the experiment-#4 engine and the accepted tapered eval was dark code. Wiring quiescentEvalBishopPair as the negamax default lands BOTH the tapered king table and the bishop-pair term.

selfPlay.note: PRIMARY A/B isolates the bishop-pair term: new = quiescentEvalBishopPair (tapered+pair), old = quiescentEvalTapered (tapered only, the accepted #5 engine). Both use quiescence + shipped check extensions + tapered king. Disjoint opening seeds. Score: win=1 draw=0.5 loss=0 for new.

depth4_uiDefault.verdict: neutral / within-noise (SE~4% over 160 games); non-regressing but not a clear gain. 4 of 8 seeds >=50%. High depth-4 seed variance, consistent with prior experiments.

review: Adversarial subagent review of the diff: all 7 correctness properties PASS (verdict SHIP). (1) backward-compat: bishopPair=false path byte-for-byte unchanged, deltaMargin exactly DELTA_MARGIN when off; (2) color symmetry: bishopPairDelta antisymmetric by construction, mirror position nets 0, lowercase=white counting correct; (3) counting: iterates the 64 real mailbox squares, >=2 captures the pair incl. 3+ from promotion; (4) delta-pruning soundness: a capture removes one ENEMY piece and auto-queens, so the pair term swings by at most +BISHOP_PAIR_BONUS (only downward on the enemy bonus), fully covered by the widened margin — and any swing co-occurs with a >=325 material gain already counted, so the widening is conservatively redundant; (5) negamax-default change safe: all 5 default-eval tests in ai.test.ts assert only structural properties or forced mates (scored structurally, independent of the leaf), none assert a flippable quiet move; (6) bishopPair threaded through stand-pat, margin, and every recursive quiesce; (7) the 3 new unit tests pin symmetry/rewards-holder/no-bonus-without-pair with valid setups. No bugs.
reason: Non-regressing at every depth the UI plays and net-positive overall across 580 seeded isolated games from varied openings, both colors: depth 2 52.5% (240g, all seeds +), depth 3 57.5% (180g, all seeds +), depth 4 51.25% (160g, neutral/within-noise), aggregate 53.7%. The isolated bishop-pair gain is real at depths 2-3 and neutral (not a regression) at the production depth 4, where the effect is swamped by high seed variance. Validated at depth 3+ per the #3 lesson. It is also a genuine correctness fix (the engine had been treating two bishops as worth exactly a bishop plus a knight). Crucially, this change also ships the accepted-but-never-wired tapered eval (#5): the production-hop confirmation shows the shipped engine beats the ACTUAL live (non-tapered) engine 58.75% over 120 games at depths 2/3/4 (incl. 62.5%/60.0% at depth 4) — so the browser AI gets clearly stronger, with the large depth-4 production gain coming from finally activating tapering. Gate all green; bundle 6.92KB brotli (far under 45KB); adversarial diff review 7/7 PASS. Unlike the rejected pawn-structure term (#3), the bishop-pair bonus induces no committal moves — it only biases equal trades toward keeping the pair — so it cannot steer the shallow search into material it cannot convert.
